observations.note: Zinc-blende reflections of the CdSe cores; page 2, Fig. 1a.

observations.value: reflections shift to higher angle after ZnS growth; no separate wurtzite or ZnS peaks
observations.note: Compared with the CdSe cores (S1); page 2, Fig. 1a.

findings.claim: The CdSe cores are zinc blende (F-43m) with a = 6.08 A.
The ZnS shell is a coherent (epitaxial) zinc-blende shell that compresses the core.

structural_constraints.property: CdSe core lattice parameter a (zinc blende)
structural_constraints.derivation: Stated for the zinc-blende CdSe cores before shelling (S1); the ZnS shell of S2 is grown on these cores and, according to the authors, compresses this lattice (O2, evidence E2).

structural_constraints.value: ZnS shell on the same zinc-blende lattice as the core
structural_constraints.derivation: The reflections shift to higher angle after ZnS growth and no separate wurtzite or ZnS peaks appear; the authors read this as a coherent (epitaxial) zinc-blende shell.

structural_constraints.value: zinc-blende CdSe core of 2.8 nm diameter with a = 6.08 A
structural_constraints.derivation: Required by the evidence. XRD gives the zinc-blende phase and a = 6.08 A of the bare cores (O1, evidence E1). Cross-technique support: the 2.8 nm core diameter is from TEM (TEM:O1, evidence E3).

structural_constraints.value: coherent zinc-blende ZnS shell of about two monolayers, overall diameter 3.9 nm
structural_constraints.derivation: Required by the evidence. The XRD reflections shift to higher angle after shelling with no separate wurtzite or ZnS peaks (O2, evidence E2). Cross-technique support: TEM gives the 3.9 nm overall diameter and about 0.55 nm (two monolayers) of ZnS (TEM:O2, evidence E4); the ICP-OES Zn:Cd ratio of 1.6 is consistent with two ZnS monolayers (ICP-OES:O1, evidence E5).

caveats: Not provided by the paper: ZnS lattice strain profile (strain distribution in the shell).
